definitions.explanation: The person who first established or created something, such as a company, organization, school of thought, or movement.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{創始者|そうししゃ}は{誰|だれ}ですか。
examples.english: Who is the founder of the company?

examples.japanese: この{宗教|しゅうきょう}の{創始者|そうししゃ}は{千年以上前|せんねんいじょうまえ}に{生|う}まれた。
examples.english: The founder of this religion was born over a thousand years ago.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はその{武道|ぶどう}の{創始者|そうししゃ}として{世界中|せかいじゅう}で{尊敬|そんけい}されている。
examples.english: He is respected around the world as the founder of that martial art.

notes:
Refers to the person who first brought something into existence. Unlike {設立者|せつりつしゃ} which focuses on the formal act of establishing an organization, {創始者|そうししゃ} emphasizes the creative or pioneering aspect of starting something new.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {会社|かいしゃ}の{創始者|そうししゃ}: founder of a company
- {宗教|しゅうきょう}の{創始者|そうししゃ}: founder of a religion
- {流派|りゅうは}の{創始者|そうししゃ}: founder of a school (of martial arts, art, etc.)
- {運動|うんどう}の{創始者|そうししゃ}: originator of a movement

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {設立者|せつりつしゃ}: focuses on the formal, institutional act of establishing something (a corporation, foundation)
- {開祖|かいそ}: founder of a religious sect or martial arts school; carries a more traditional, reverential tone
- {創業者|そうぎょうしゃ}: specifically a business founder who started a commercial enterprise
